To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the capacity of a mobile multiple-antenna communication link in Rayl eigh flat fading is achieved when the transmitted signal matrix is a product of a unitary matrix and a certain random matrix that is real, nonnegative, and diagonal; and that, for a given number of transmit t er and receive antennas, the capacity increases with the length of the channel coherence interval and appr oaches that achieved when the receiver has perfect knowledge of the channel.
the capacity of a multiple-antenna link is achieved when the transmitted signal is the product of a unitary matrix and a certain diagonal matrix.

the capacity of a mobile multiple-antenna communication link is equal to the capa city of an equivalent link that has the same number of antennas as the length of a coherence interval, and that this capacity can be achieved by a transmission scheme that is the product of two matrices: one that is isotropically distributed and unitary, the other that is diagonal, random, and nonnegative.

the problem of communicating over a mobile wireless link with M transmit antennas and N receive antennas.
the capacity of a mobile multiple-antenna link.
the capacity of multiple-antenna wireless links in Rayleigh flat-fadding channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the presence of fading, a mobile link withM transmitter and N receiver antennas has a capacity of log(1 + SNR), whereSNR is the signal-t o-noise power ratio, and that this capacity is achieved when the M N transmitted signals are chosen i ndependently and identically distributed, and with a distribution which depends on the length of the fading interval.
, for a given number of antennas, the capacity of a mobile wireless link in Rayleigh flat-fade is achieved when the transmitter sends the same number of symbols as the length of a fading interval.

the capacity of a mobile wireless link is equal to the maximum of the capacity of the channel when the receiver knows the propagation coefficients and the capacity of the same channel in which the receiver does not know the propagation coefficients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, if you have M transmitter and N rec eiver antennas and the propagation coefficients are constant for T symbol periods, then the capacity is equal to the number of degrees of freedom, T M N, times the capacity per degree of freedom.
the capacity of the link is achieved by a transmission that is independent of the propagation coefficients and that is a function of only the coherence interval.
, in a Rayleigh fading environment, the capacity of a mobile wireless link with M transmitter and N receiver antennas is achieved by using M = N = T transmit antennas.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the capacity of a mobile wireless link with M transmit ter and N receive antennas is equal to the maximum of the following two quantities: (i) the capacity of a link with T transmit and T receive antennas, whereT is the length of a coherence interval, and (ii) the capacity of an ideal link with M transmit and N receive antennas in which the receiver knows the propagation coefficients exactly.

the capacity of a mobile wireless link is equal to the c apacity of a link in which the receiver has complete channel state information (CSI) when the numbe r of transmitter antennas is equal to the length of the fading interval.
